title: Cloud-Native Revolution: Harmonic VOS and Red Hat OpenShift Mastering Video Delivery, Cost, and Scale
body_html:
What Was Announced

Harmonic, a leading provider of video delivery and cloud media processing solutions, has announced a partnership with Red Hat to integrate Harmonic's cloud-native video operating system (VOS) with Red Hat OpenShift, a container application platform. This integration aims to simplify the deployment, integration, and scaling of video delivery workflows, enabling media teams to reduce operational complexity and improve efficiency. The partnership combines Harmonic's VOS, a cloud-native video processing platform, with Red Hat OpenShift, a container application platform that provides a flexible and scalable infrastructure for deploying and managing applications. This integration enables media teams to deploy and manage video delivery workflows as cloud-native applications, leveraging the benefits of containerization and orchestration.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The integration of Harmonic's VOS with Red Hat OpenShift has significant engineering and operational implications for media teams. By deploying video delivery workflows as cloud-native applications, teams can simplify the management of complex workflows, reduce the risk of errors, and improve the overall efficiency of their operations. This is particularly important for media teams that are under pressure to deliver high-quality content to multiple platforms, including OTT, social media, and traditional broadcast. The integration also enables teams to take advantage of the scalability and flexibility of cloud-native applications, which can be easily scaled up or down to meet changing demand. This is particularly important for media teams that need to handle large volumes of content and deliver it to multiple platforms. By leveraging the benefits of cloud-native applications, teams can reduce the complexity of their operations, improve their ability to respond to changing demand, and deliver high-quality content to their audiences. Furthermore, the integration of Harmonic's VOS with Red Hat OpenShift provides a common platform for managing video delivery workflows, which can help to reduce the complexity of operations and improve the overall efficiency of media teams. By leveraging a common platform, teams can simplify the management of their workflows, reduce the risk of errors, and improve their ability to respond to changing demand.

Industry Context

The integration of Harmonic's VOS with Red Hat OpenShift is part of a broader trend in the media industry towards the adoption of cloud-native applications and software-defined workflows. This trend is driven by the need for media teams to simplify their operations, improve their efficiency, and reduce their costs. By leveraging the benefits of cloud-native applications and software-defined workflows, media teams can reduce the complexity of their operations, improve their ability to respond to changing demand, and deliver high-quality content to their audiences. Other companies, such as AWS Elemental and Kaltura, have also developed cloud-native video processing platforms that provide similar benefits to media teams. These platforms enable teams to deploy and manage video delivery workflows as cloud-native applications, leveraging the benefits of containerization and orchestration. However, the integration of Harmonic's VOS with Red Hat OpenShift provides a unique combination of video processing and container application platform capabilities, which can help to simplify the management of complex workflows and improve the overall efficiency of media teams.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

For broadcast and media teams, the integration of Harmonic's VOS with Red Hat OpenShift has significant implications for their operations. Teams should consider the benefits of deploying video delivery workflows as cloud-native applications, including the simplification of operations, the improvement of efficiency, and the reduction of costs. They should also consider the need to develop the skills and expertise required to manage cloud-native applications and software-defined workflows. Furthermore, teams should evaluate the integration of Harmonic's VOS with Red Hat OpenShift against their specific operational needs and workflows. They should consider the benefits of a common platform for managing video delivery workflows, including the simplification of operations and the improvement of efficiency. They should also consider the need to develop a strategy for managing the transition to cloud-native applications and software-defined workflows, including the development of new skills and expertise. Ultimately, the integration of Harmonic's VOS with Red Hat OpenShift provides a unique opportunity for broadcast and media teams to simplify their operations, improve their efficiency, and reduce their costs. By leveraging the benefits of cloud-native applications and software-defined workflows, teams can deliver high-quality content to their audiences, improve their ability to respond to changing demand, and reduce the complexity of their operations.
